convoLines.text: "My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Spool? I'm pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"...Mm. Sorry. Say that again? I was somewhere better."
They nod. "Okay."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know the old burn east of camp — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Spool? Tyler is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. I wanted to ask rather than assume."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind this wound — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
Tyler seems lighter — something good landed recently.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"No, really — it's handled. Thanks for asking, though."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Water's almost gone — 3 liters. I can't carry enough alone. First light, the creek, you and me?"
"Do the math with me: 3 liters, 8 people. That's not tomorrow's water. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. You don't know what it's like, being the only nobody in a camp of somebodies."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that water haul."
Nancy looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Nancy rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
They light up a little when they see you.
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"Still on what's been happening."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Tyler grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Maybe — Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Nancy doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"Caleb is gone and Raj is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I wake before anyone else. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"The fire feels smaller without Raj. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening."

"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Now then — What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"Fine — The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"Still on what you did for fun."

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Let's see — The others think I've got it together. Cute. Very cute."
"I wonder if Vladivostok, Russia misses me. Stupid. Places don't miss people. ...Do they?"
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Emma Kraemer is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Emma Kraemer is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Emma kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Emma's gone." Tyler looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Emma." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Linh blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Scrounger (Level 1). Ruin looting finds +1 item.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Emma Kraemer, 41 days. The mantle passes to Linh Walker.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Linh Walker, 42 — a chimney sweep. Their hands know different work now: Iron Stomach, Green Whisper, Green Thumb, Literally.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Emma — and Emma is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Tyler, Nancy, Tancredi and 5 more speak for Linh — "Emma trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Linh before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
